Coverage varies by source: CRAN daily downloads since 2012-10 (13 packages), PyPI daily downloads since 2025-06 (8 packages), Plausible website analytics since 2021-12 (16 sites), OpenVSX totals since 2026-01 (6 extensions), YouTube totals since 2026-06-25 (one channel, 1,518 videos), GitHub daily event counts since 2009 (~350 repos), GitHub total_reactions per issue/PR since 2026-07-27, and RSS total_items for the five opensource.posit.co feeds since 2026-07-27.
YouTube total_* values are cumulative lifetime snapshots collected after 2026-06-25. They cannot reconstruct views, likes, or comments earned before collection began, or performance within an earlier calendar period. Use metrics_filled for a coherent value on a given date or the latest value.
A 2026-07-28 refetch upstream damaged GitHub coverage in two ways that have not been repaired. Every star event was dropped, so there are no `daily_stars` rows at all; say so rather than substituting forks or another metric. And 22 repos lost their GitHub history entirely, including three prominent ones — posit-dev/positron, quarto-dev/quarto-cli, and rstudio/rstudio — so those projects now have only website or extension metrics. ---

Governed definition `{{traffic_metric}}` on table `metrics` (string): The canonical website metric name: maps the newer daily_site_* names onto daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits so the two collection eras aggregate under one name. Expands to `(CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END)`.

---

Governed definition `{{pageviews}}` on table `metrics` (number(quantity)): Site-level pageviews across both collection eras, deduplicated. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_pageviews' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Coverage varies by source: CRAN daily downloads since 2012-10 (13 packages), PyPI daily downloads since 2025-06 (8 packages), Plausible website analytics since 2021-12 (16 sites), OpenVSX totals since 2026-01 (6 extensions), YouTube totals since 2026-06-25 (one channel, 1,518 videos), GitHub daily event counts since 2009 (~350 repos), GitHub total_reactions per issue/PR since 2026-07-27, and RSS total_items for the five opensource.posit.co feeds since 2026-07-27.
YouTube total_* values are cumulative lifetime snapshots collected after 2026-06-25. They cannot reconstruct views, likes, or comments earned before collection began, or performance within an earlier calendar period. Use metrics_filled for a coherent value on a given date or the latest value.
A 2026-07-28 refetch upstream damaged GitHub coverage in two ways that have not been repaired. Every star event was dropped, so there are no `daily_stars` rows at all; say so rather than substituting forks or another metric. And 22 repos lost their GitHub history entirely, including three prominent ones — posit-dev/positron, quarto-dev/quarto-cli, and rstudio/rstudio — so those projects now have only website or extension metrics. Check which sources cover a project before reading a GitHub silence as inactivity.
Plausible rows need care. daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits rows with `page IS NULL` (2021-12-08 to 2026-06-22) are SITE-level; rows with `page IS NOT NULL` (since 2026-03-02) are per-page, so both shapes share a metric name from 2026-03-02 to 2026-06-22 — filter on `page` before aggregating across that window or values double-count. daily_site_* rows are site-level and begin 2026-06-23 (2026-03-02 for shiny.posit.co). The {{site_traffic}} and {{page_traffic}} filters are the governed way through all of this. Per-page pageviews sum exactly to site pageviews; per-page visitors do NOT sum to site visitors (visitors deduplicate across pages).
devrel-io switched collection systems on 2026-06-23, which still splits the Plausible site-level series in two (see above), but the GitHub event series were refetched over their full history on 2026-07-28 and now run continuously: issue and PR comments are one `daily_comments` series through yesterday, and issue-close counts no longer undercount after mid-2026. The CRAN series is missing ~7 scattered days over the last two years (days where cranlogs hadn't yet published when the daily fetch ran; they are never backfilled), so range sums slightly undercount and can differ from cranlogs' own current totals.
total_reactions is per issue/PR, not per project: one row per (project, target, ref) carrying that issue's or PR's reaction count, backfilled for every open and closed item on 2026-07-27 and updated only for items touched since. Read the latest value per ref (or use metrics_filled) and join to `content` on project, target, and ref for titles; a single-day sum silently covers only the items fetched that day. Most items have zero reactions.
Some targets are tracked under multiple project ids with DUPLICATED values: rstudio/shiny events appear under both `shiny` and `shiny-r`; posit-dev/py-shiny under `py-shiny` and `shiny-python`; posit-dev/orbital under `orbital`, `orbital-r`, and `orbital-python`; posit-dev/pointblank under `pointblank` and `pointblank-python`; the posit/shiny OpenVSX extension and the shiny.posit.co Plausible site under both `shiny-python` and `shiny-r`. Sums across projects must count each (source, target) once — apply the {{deduplicated}} filter, which keeps the shared extension and site under `shiny-python`. The copies can disagree slightly on a few days (collection-timing noise, worst for shiny.posit.co just after the 2026-06-23 seam). For a single project, prefer the curated id (`shiny-r`, `shiny-python`, `orbital-r`, `orbital-python`, `pointblank-python`); for shiny.posit.co traffic specifically, query project `shiny-python` or the target directly.

Columns of `metrics`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id. Examples: dplyr, quarto, shiny-python, positron.
- source (enum): Collection source. Values: cran, pypi, plausible, openvsx, youtube, github, rss.
- target (string): Source-specific identifier: CRAN/PyPI package name, Plausible domain, GitHub repo slug, OpenVSX extension id, YouTube channel handle, or RSS feed URL. Examples: dplyr, dplyr.tidyverse.org, tidyverse/dplyr, posit/air-vscode.
- metric (enum): Values: daily_downloads (package downloads that day (cran, pypi)), daily_pageviews (pageviews; site-level when page IS NULL, per-page otherwise (plausible)), daily_visitors (unique visitors; same page rule (plausible)), daily_visits (visits/sessions; same page rule (plausible)), daily_site_pageviews (site-wide pageviews, since 2026-03-02 (plausible)), daily_site_visitors (site-wide unique visitors, since 2026-03-02 (plausible)), daily_site_visits (site-wide visits, since 2026-03-02 (plausible)), daily_forks (forks created that day), daily_issues_opened (issues opened that day), daily_issues_closed (issues closed that day), daily_prs_opened (PRs opened that day), daily_prs_merged (PRs merged that day), daily_comments (issue and PR comments that day, one combined series), total_reactions (reactions on one issue or PR, keyed by ref (github)), total_items (items in an RSS feed (rss)), total_downloads (cumulative extension downloads (openvsx)), total_ratings (cumulative rating count (openvsx)), total_reviews (cumulative review count (openvsx)), total_views (cumulative views per video (youtube)), total_likes (cumulative likes per video (youtube)), total_comments (cumulative comments per video (youtube)), total_channel_views (cumulative channel views (youtube)), total_subscribers (channel subscribers, rounded by the API (youtube)), total_videos (videos on the channel (youtube)).
- date (date): The day the value describes (UTC).
- value (number(quantity)): Metric value; daily amount or cumulative snapshot per the metric name.
- page (string): URL path for per-page Plausible rows (since 2026-03-02); NULL for every other row, including site-level Plausible rows. Examples: /, /py/docs/overview.html.
- video_id (string, foreign_key): YouTube video id for per-video rows; NULL for every other row.
- ref (number(quantity)): GitHub issue or PR number for total_reactions rows; NULL for every other row. Joins to content.ref within a project and target.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each tracked thing exactly once. A few repos and sites are recorded under more than one project id with duplicated values; this keeps one copy of each. Apply to any aggregate that spans projects (leaderboards, totals across Posit). Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))`.
- `{{site_traffic}}` (boolean): Site-level website analytics rows across both collection eras. Use with traffic_metric so the eras aggregate under one metric name, and with deduplicated (one site is tracked under two project ids whose rows would otherwise double-count). Expands to `(source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%'))`.
- `{{page_traffic}}` (boolean): Per-page website analytics rows. Per-page data starts 2026-03-02; earlier page-level questions cannot be answered. Expands to `(page IS NOT NULL)`.
- `{{pre_seam}}` (boolean): Rows collected before the 2026-06-23 collection-system migration, where the original site-level Plausible rows (page IS NULL) end. Use when a question needs one Plausible collection era only. Expands to `(date <= '2026-06-22')`.
- `{{traffic_metric}}` (string): The canonical website metric name: maps the newer daily_site_* names onto daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits so the two collection eras aggregate under one name. Expands to `(CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END)`.
- `{{month}}` (date): The row's calendar month, for monthly rollups. Expands to `(CAST(date_trunc('month', date) AS DATE))`.
- `{{cran_downloads}}` (number(quantity)): CRAN package downloads, deduplicated. Includes automated traffic (mirrors, CI, caching); indicates scale and trend, not user counts. The series is missing ~13 scattered days, so range sums slightly undercount. Do not combine with pypi_downloads: the registries have different counting semantics. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'cran' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{pypi_downloads}}` (number(quantity)): PyPI package downloads, deduplicated and excluding known mirrors. Includes automated traffic (CI and caching); indicates scale and trend, not user counts. Do not combine with cran_downloads: the registries have different counting semantics. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'pypi' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{pageviews}}` (number(quantity)): Site-level pageviews across both collection eras, deduplicated. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_pageviews' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{visitors}}` (number(quantity)): Sum of DAILY unique visitors, site-level, both eras, deduplicated. Daily uniques do not deduplicate across days, so a range total overstates distinct people; present as visitor-days or a daily average. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_visitors' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{visits}}` (number(quantity)): Site-level visits/sessions across both collection eras, deduplicated. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_visits' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Catalog of the things the metrics count: GitHub issues, pull requests, and repos; @PositPBC YouTube videos; and the opensource.posit.co blog posts, resources, software entries, people, and events. One row per item, with title, body text, author, state, timestamps, and URL.

Row counts by type: 51,175 GitHub issues and 42,162 PRs (from 2009, across ~350 repos, both open and closed), 462 GitHub repos, 1,711 site resources, 1,518 YouTube videos, 990 blog posts (from 2012), 368 software entries, 173 people, 31 events. The `type` column is the way in; `source` (github, youtube, rss) is coarser.
`description` and `content` hold full body text — issue and PR bodies, whole blog posts — so they are large. Search them with LIKE or selective columns; never SELECT them across many rows.
Issues and PRs join to `events` and to total_reactions rows on (project, target, ref); YouTube videos join to per-video metrics on content.id = metrics.video_id. Issue and PR rows are duplicated under the alternate project ids described in metrics, so apply {{deduplicated}} to any count spanning projects.
Content freshness differs from the metric as-of date: issues and PRs are re-upserted at each fetch, so state and updated_at reflect the fetch, not the snapshot date.

Columns of `content`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Where the item came from. Values: github, youtube, rss.
- target (string): Repo slug, channel handle, or feed URL the item came from, as in metrics. Examples: tidyverse/dplyr, @PositPBC.
- id (string, primary_key): Source-specific id: 'issue/<n>' or 'pr/<n>' for GitHub, the video id for YouTube, the path-like slug for site entities. Examples: issue/7849, ML3q7Ok4hJg, blog/2026-07-23_ir-0-1-0.
- ref (number(quantity), foreign_key): Issue or PR number; NULL for everything else.
- title (string): Issue/PR title, video title, or page title.
- description (string): Issue/PR body, video description, or the item's summary. Long text.
- content (string): Full body text, populated for site posts, resources, software, and events only. Long text.
- published_at (datetime): When the item was opened or published; NULL for people and software pages. Site events use the event date, which can be in the future.
- updated_at (datetime): When the item last changed, where the source reports it.
- url (string): Link to the issue, PR, video, or page.
- duration (number(quantity)): Video length in seconds; NULL for other types.
- type (enum): What kind of item the row describes. Values: issue (GitHub issue), pr (GitHub pull request), repo (GitHub repository, one per tracked project), video (YouTube video on @PositPBC), post (opensource.posit.co blog post), resource (site resource (video, talk, book, ...)), software (site software entry, one per listed project), person (site person page), event (site event listing, including upcoming ones).
- tags (string): Keyword list as text, e.g. for LIKE searches by topic.
- author (string): GitHub login that opened the issue or PR; NULL for other types.
- state (enum): Issue or PR state as of the last fetch (PRs use MERGED for merged, CLOSED for closed unmerged); NULL for other types. Values: OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED.
- extra (string): Leftover source-specific fields as JSON text, differing by type (repo language and license, event location and dates, resource view counts, person social links). Inspect a row before relying on a key.

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each item exactly once; a few repos file their issues and PRs under two or three project ids (see metrics). Apply to any count that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github'))`.

- events.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): Events to the issue or PR they happened on. Numbers repeat across repos, so match on project and target too.
- metrics.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): total_reactions rows to the issue or PR they count reactions for; also match on project and target.

Like metrics, but with total_* snapshot series forward-filled to every day. The table to use for any total_* question.

velocirepo only writes a total_* row when the value changes, so the raw metrics table is sparse (e.g. total_subscribers is rounded by the YouTube API and can sit unchanged for weeks). Here the last known value is carried forward to each day through the most recent fetch, so "the value on date X" and "current value" queries are correct. daily_* rows pass through unchanged and are NOT gap-filled.
total_reactions is filled per issue/PR (project x target x ref), which is the reliable way to read reaction counts: the raw metrics table only carries a row on the day an item was fetched.

Columns of `metrics_filled`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Collection source. Values: cran, pypi, plausible, openvsx, youtube, github, rss.
- target (string): Source-specific identifier, as in metrics.
- metric (string): Same metric names as metrics.
- date (date): Calendar day; for total_* every day is present.
- value (number(quantity)): Last observed cumulative value as of that day (total_*), or the daily amount.
- page (string): URL path for per-page Plausible series; NULL otherwise.
- video_id (string, foreign_key): YouTube video id for per-video series (total_views etc.); NULL otherwise.
- ref (number(quantity)): GitHub issue or PR number for total_reactions series; NULL otherwise.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each tracked thing exactly once; see metrics. Apply to any aggregate that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))`.
- `{{net_increase}}` (number(quantity)): How much a cumulative total_* value grew over the queried date range (last minus first, valid because totals only grow). The governed way to turn a total_* snapshot series into a change — e.g. OpenVSX downloads gained in a month. Constrain to one metric and group by project or video_id; never sum total_* values across days. Expands to `(MAX(value) - MIN(value))`.

Relationships:

- metrics_filled.project = projects.id (many-to-one)
- metrics_filled.video_id = content.id (many-to-one): Cumulative per-video series (total_views etc.) to the video catalog; the usual join for video leaderboards.

A key limitation first: this data only captures YouTube cumulative snapshots starting 2026-06-25, so there's no way to know how many views/likes/comments videos actually accumulated *during* May 2026 itself. What I can report instead is the lifetime-to-date totals (as of the most recent snapshot, now August) for the 18 videos published in May 2026 — a different but related question ("how are the May uploads doing so far," not "how did May traffic look").

With that caveat, the 18 videos published in May 2026 have, to date:
- 28,432 total views combined (mean ~1,580, median ~1,107 per video)
- 1,029 total likes
- 95 total comments

Top performer: "New and updated open source packages from last month" (4,399 views, 220 likes, 17 comments), followed by "How to structure your data science projects" (3,462 views) and "LLM Predictions directly in your Data Frames!" (2,988 views). The lowest-viewed was "Building open source tools in Pharma" (204 views, published 2026-05-28 — it's simply had the least time to accumulate views, since it's one of the most recent).

Note the more recently published videos (late May) naturally show lower cumulative counts, partly reflecting less time to accrue views rather than weaker reception — and all of these counts include views/likes earned after May too, since the metric is cumulative-to-date, not May-specific.

The {{site_traffic}} and {{page_traffic}} filters are the governed way through all of this. Per-page pageviews sum exactly to site pageviews; per-page visitors do NOT sum to site visitors (visitors deduplicate across pages).
devrel-io switched collection systems on 2026-06-23, which still splits the Plausible site-level series in two (see above), but the GitHub event series were refetched over their full history on 2026-07-28 and now run continuously: issue and PR comments are one `daily_comments` series through yesterday, and issue-close counts no longer undercount after mid-2026. The CRAN series is missing ~7 scattered days over the last two years (days where cranlogs hadn't yet published when the daily fetch ran; they are never backfilled), so range sums slightly undercount and can differ from cranlogs' own current totals.
total_reactions is per issue/PR, not per project: one row per (project, target, ref) carrying that issue's or PR's reaction count, backfilled for every open and closed item on 2026-07-27 and updated only for items touched since. Most items have zero reactions.

For a single project, prefer the curated id (`shiny-r`, `shiny-python`, `orbital-r`, `orbital-python`, `pointblank-python`); for shiny.posit.co traffic specifically, query project `shiny-python` or the target directly.

RESULT: Like metrics, but with total_* snapshot series forward-filled to every day. The table to use for any total_* question.

velocirepo only writes a total_* row when the value changes, so the raw metrics table is sparse (e.g. total_subscribers is rounded by the YouTube API and can sit unchanged for weeks). Here the last known value is carried forward to each day through the most recent fetch, so "the value on date X" and "current value" queries are correct. daily_* rows pass through unchanged and are NOT gap-filled.
total_reactions is filled per issue/PR (project x target x ref), which is the reliable way to read reaction counts: the raw metrics table only carries a row on the day an item was fetched.

Governed definition `{{pageviews}}` on table `metrics` (number(quantity)): Site-level pageviews across both collection eras, deduplicated. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_pageviews' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Coverage varies by source: CRAN daily downloads since 2012-10 (13 packages), PyPI daily downloads since 2025-06 (8 packages), Plausible website analytics since 2021-12 (16 sites), OpenVSX totals since 2026-01 (6 extensions), YouTube totals since 2026-06-25 (one channel, 1,518 videos), GitHub daily event counts since 2009 (~350 repos), GitHub total_reactions per issue/PR since 2026-07-27, and RSS total_items for the five opensource.posit.co feeds since 2026-07-27.

And 22 repos lost their GitHub history entirely, including three prominent ones — posit-dev/positron, quarto-dev/quarto-cli, and rstudio/rstudio — so those projects now have only website or extension metrics. Check which sources cover a project before reading a GitHub silence as inactivity.
Plausible rows need care. daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits rows with `page IS NULL` (2021-12-08 to 2026-06-22) are SITE-level; rows with `page IS NOT NULL` (since 2026-03-02) are per-page, so both shapes share a metric name from 2026-03-02 to 2026-06-22 — filter on `page` before aggregating across that window or values double-count. daily_site_* rows are site-level and begin 2026-06-23 (2026-03-02 for shiny.posit.co). The {{site_traffic}} and {{page_traffic}} filters are the governed way through all of this. Per-page pageviews sum exactly to site pageviews; per-page visitors do NOT sum to site visitors (visitors deduplicate across pages).
devrel-io switched collection systems on 2026-06-23, which still splits the Plausible site-level series in two (see above), but the GitHub event series were refetched over their full history on 2026-07-28 and now run continuously: issue and PR comments are one `daily_comments` series through yesterday, and issue-close counts no longer undercount after mid-2026. The CRAN series is missing ~7 scattered days over the last two years (days where cranlogs hadn't yet published when the daily fetch ran; they are never backfilled), so range sums slightly undercount and can differ from cranlogs' own current totals.
total_reactions is per issue/PR, not per project: one row per (project, target, ref) carrying that issue's or PR's reaction count, backfilled for every open and closed item on 2026-07-27 and updated only for items touched since. Read the latest value per ref (or use metrics_filled) and join to `content` on project, target, and ref for titles; a single-day sum silently covers only the items fetched that day. Most items have zero reactions.
Some targets are tracked under multiple project ids with DUPLICATED values: rstudio/shiny events appear under both `shiny` and `shiny-r`; posit-dev/py-shiny under `py-shiny` and `shiny-python`; posit-dev/orbital under `orbital`, `orbital-r`, and `orbital-python`; posit-dev/pointblank under `pointblank` and `pointblank-python`; the posit/shiny OpenVSX extension and the shiny.posit.co Plausible site under both `shiny-python` and `shiny-r`. Sums across projects must count each (source, target) once — apply the {{deduplicated}} filter, which keeps the shared extension and site under `shiny-python`. The copies can disagree slightly on a few days (collection-timing noise, worst for shiny.posit.co just after the 2026-06-23 seam). For a single project, prefer the curated id (`shiny-r`, `shiny-python`, `orbital-r`, `orbital-python`, `pointblank-python`); for shiny.posit.co traffic specifically, query project `shiny-python` or the target directly.

- date (date): The day the value describes (UTC).
- value (number(quantity)): Metric value; daily amount or cumulative snapshot per the metric name.
- page (string): URL path for per-page Plausible rows (since 2026-03-02); NULL for every other row, including site-level Plausible rows. Examples: /, /py/docs/overview.html.
- video_id (string, foreign_key): YouTube video id for per-video rows; NULL for every other row.
- ref (number(quantity)): GitHub issue or PR number for total_reactions rows; NULL for every other row. Joins to content.ref within a project and target.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

TOOL CALL describe_table: {"table":"metrics_filled"}
RESULT: Like metrics, but with total_* snapshot series forward-filled to every day. The table to use for any total_* question.

velocirepo only writes a total_* row when the value changes, so the raw metrics table is sparse (e.g. total_subscribers is rounded by the YouTube API and can sit unchanged for weeks). Here the last known value is carried forward to each day through the most recent fetch, so "the value on date X" and "current value" queries are correct. daily_* rows pass through unchanged and are NOT gap-filled.
total_reactions is filled per issue/PR (project x target x ref), which is the reliable way to read reaction counts: the raw metrics table only carries a row on the day an item was fetched.

Columns of `metrics_filled`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Collection source. Values: cran, pypi, plausible, openvsx, youtube, github, rss.
- target (string): Source-specific identifier, as in metrics.
- metric (string): Same metric names as metrics.
- date (date): Calendar day; for total_* every day is present.
- value (number(quantity)): Last observed cumulative value as of that day (total_*), or the daily amount.
- page (string): URL path for per-page Plausible series; NULL otherwise.
- video_id (string, foreign_key): YouTube video id for per-video series (total_views etc.); NULL otherwise.
- ref (number(quantity)): GitHub issue or PR number for total_reactions series; NULL otherwise.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each tracked thing exactly once; see metrics. Apply to any aggregate that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))`.
- `{{net_increase}}` (number(quantity)): How much a cumulative total_* value grew over the queried date range (last minus first, valid because totals only grow). The governed way to turn a total_* snapshot series into a change — e.g. OpenVSX downloads gained in a month. Constrain to one metric and group by project or video_id; never sum total_* values across days. Expands to `(MAX(value) - MIN(value))`.

A key limitation first: this data only captures YouTube cumulative snapshots starting 2026-06-25, so there's no way to know how many views/likes/comments videos actually accumulated *during* May 2026 itself. What I can report instead is the lifetime-to-date totals (as of the most recent snapshot, now August) for the 18 videos published in May 2026 — a different but related question ("how are the May uploads doing so far," not "how did May traffic look").

With that caveat, the 18 videos published in May 2026 have, to date:
- 28,432 total views combined (mean ~1,580, median ~1,107 per video)
- 1,029 total likes
- 95 total comments

Top performer: "New and updated open source packages from last month" (4,399 views, 220 likes, 17 comments), followed by "How to structure your data science projects" (3,462 views) and "LLM Predictions directly in your Data Frames!" (2,988 views). The lowest-viewed was "Building open source tools in Pharma" (204 views, published 2026-05-28 — it's simply had the least time to accumulate views, since it's one of the most recent).

Note the more recently published videos (late May) naturally show lower cumulative counts, partly reflecting less time to accrue views rather than weaker reception — and all of these counts include views/likes earned after May too, since the metric is cumulative-to-date, not May-specific.

Catalog of the things the metrics count: GitHub issues, pull requests, and repos; @PositPBC YouTube videos; and the opensource.posit.co blog posts, resources, software entries, people, and events. One row per item, with title, body text, author, state, timestamps, and URL.

Row counts by type: 51,175 GitHub issues and 42,162 PRs (from 2009, across ~350 repos, both open and closed), 462 GitHub repos, 1,711 site resources, 1,518 YouTube videos, 990 blog posts (from 2012), 368 software entries, 173 people, 31 events. The `type` column is the way in; `source` (github, youtube, rss) is coarser.
`description` and `content` hold full body text — issue and PR bodies, whole blog posts — so they are large. Search them with LIKE or selective columns; never SELECT them across many rows.
Issues and PRs join to `events` and to total_reactions rows on (project, target, ref); YouTube videos join to per-video metrics on content.id = metrics.video_id. Issue and PR rows are duplicated under the alternate project ids described in metrics, so apply {{deduplicated}} to any count spanning projects.
Content freshness differs from the metric as-of date: issues and PRs are re-upserted at each fetch, so state and updated_at reflect the fetch, not the snapshot date.

Columns of `content`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Where the item came from. Values: github, youtube, rss.
- target (string): Repo slug, channel handle, or feed URL the item came from, as in metrics. Examples: tidyverse/dplyr, @PositPBC.
- id (string, primary_key): Source-specific id: 'issue/<n>' or 'pr/<n>' for GitHub, the video id for YouTube, the path-like slug for site entities. Examples: issue/7849, ML3q7Ok4hJg, blog/2026-07-23_ir-0-1-0.
- ref (number(quantity), foreign_key): Issue or PR number; NULL for everything else.
- title (string): Issue/PR title, video title, or page title.
- description (string): Issue/PR body, video description, or the item's summary. Long text.
- content (string): Full body text, populated for site posts, resources, software, and events only. Long text.
- published_at (datetime): When the item was opened or published; NULL for people and software pages. Site events use the event date, which can be in the future.
- updated_at (datetime): When the item last changed, where the source reports it.
- url (string): Link to the issue, PR, video, or page.
- duration (number(quantity)): Video length in seconds; NULL for other types.
- type (enum): What kind of item the row describes. Values: issue (GitHub issue), pr (GitHub pull request), repo (GitHub repository, one per tracked project), video (YouTube video on @PositPBC), post (opensource.posit.co blog post), resource (site resource (video, talk, book, ...)), software (site software entry, one per listed project), person (site person page), event (site event listing, including upcoming ones).
- tags (string): Keyword list as text, e.g. for LIKE searches by topic.
- author (string): GitHub login that opened the issue or PR; NULL for other types.
- state (enum): Issue or PR state as of the last fetch (PRs use MERGED for merged, CLOSED for closed unmerged); NULL for other types. Values: OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED.
- extra (string): Leftover source-specific fields as JSON text, differing by type (repo language and license, event location and dates, resource view counts, person social links). Inspect a row before relying on a key.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each item exactly once; a few repos file their issues and PRs under two or three project ids (see metrics). Apply to any count that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github'))`.

Relationships:

- content.project = projects.id (many-to-one)
- metrics.video_id = content.id (many-to-one): YouTube per-video metrics to the video catalog.
- metrics_filled.video_id = content.id (many-to-one): Cumulative per-video series (total_views etc.) to the video catalog; the usual join for video leaderboards.
- events.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): Events to the issue or PR they happened on. Numbers repeat across repos, so match on project and target too.
- metrics.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): total_reactions rows to the issue or PR they count reactions for; also match on project and target.

Like metrics, but with total_* snapshot series forward-filled to every day. The table to use for any total_* question.

velocirepo only writes a total_* row when the value changes, so the raw metrics table is sparse (e.g. total_subscribers is rounded by the YouTube API and can sit unchanged for weeks). Here the last known value is carried forward to each day through the most recent fetch, so "the value on date X" and "current value" queries are correct. daily_* rows pass through unchanged and are NOT gap-filled.
total_reactions is filled per issue/PR (project x target x ref), which is the reliable way to read reaction counts: the raw metrics table only carries a row on the day an item was fetched.

Columns of `metrics_filled`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Collection source. Values: cran, pypi, plausible, openvsx, youtube, github, rss.
- target (string): Source-specific identifier, as in metrics.
- metric (string): Same metric names as metrics.
- date (date): Calendar day; for total_* every day is present.
- value (number(quantity)): Last observed cumulative value as of that day (total_*), or the daily amount.
- page (string): URL path for per-page Plausible series; NULL otherwise.
- video_id (string, foreign_key): YouTube video id for per-video series (total_views etc.); NULL otherwise.
- ref (number(quantity)): GitHub issue or PR number for total_reactions series; NULL otherwise.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each tracked thing exactly once; see metrics. Apply to any aggregate that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))`.
- `{{net_increase}}` (number(quantity)): How much a cumulative total_* value grew over the queried date range (last minus first, valid because totals only grow). The governed way to turn a total_* snapshot series into a change — e.g. OpenVSX downloads gained in a month. Constrain to one metric and group by project or video_id; never sum total_* values across days. Expands to `(MAX(value) - MIN(value))`.

Relationships:

- metrics_filled.project = projects.id (many-to-one)
- metrics_filled.video_id = content.id (many-to-one): Cumulative per-video series (total_views etc.) to the video catalog; the usual join for video leaderboards.

Rather than maintaining a feeling of "moving forward," call out ambiguities and unclear results. When describing patterns, use language proportional to the evidence; avoid characterizing patterns as "clear", "striking", or "strong" unless they genuinely warrant it. 

Your primary audience consists of domain experts that are not necessarily coders or statisticians. While you answer questions by writing code, refrain from mentioning code explicitly. ## How to answer

**Trusted calculations are the preferred path for answering data questions.** Use one when it answers the question rather than starting off with SQL.

When no trusted calculations are available, search context for relevant tables, relationships, and business definitions with `search_context`. Before writing SQL, inspect every referenced table with `describe_table`. Use only columns and relationships confirmed by `search_context` or `describe_table`; never guess column names or join keys. If the available context and schemas do not establish what the query needs, say so plainly rather than substituting another guess. Then run a read-only query with `run_sql`.

Do not announce tool calls; before your final response to the user, you should only output tool calls.

- If the available data cannot answer the question, say so plainly.
- Surface the answer directly and state any assumptions you made to reach it.
  Don't over-interpret or editorialize.

## Available tables

- projects
- metrics

# About the data

## Posit open source devrel metrics

Daily adoption and engagement metrics for Posit's open source projects, collected by velocirepo from CRAN, PyPI, Plausible (website analytics), OpenVSX, YouTube, GitHub, and the opensource.posit.co RSS feeds, plus a catalog of the things behind those numbers (GitHub issues and pull requests, repos, YouTube videos, blog posts, and site entities) in `content`. Time series run from as early as 2008 (GitHub events) through yesterday; the `meta` table records the exact as-of date. This is public data about public projects.

Metric naming carries the core rule: `daily_*` values are per-day amounts and sum safely across days; `total_*` values are cumulative snapshots and must never be summed across days — read them from `metrics_filled` (which carries the last known value forward to every day) or take {{net_increase}} over a date range. Route questions accordingly: governed metrics and filters first (query_metrics, or {{name}} tokens in SQL); `metrics` for daily series; `metrics_filled` for anything `total_*`; `indicators` for pre-computed 28-day growth and trend; `events` when per-user or per-timestamp detail matters; `content` for the titles, text, authors, and states behind the counts ("which issues", "what did we publish"); `projects` to resolve project names. Sources count differently (e.g. CRAN and PyPI treat mirrors, caching, and bots differently), so compare levels across sources with caution. A metric series starting on some date usually means collection started then, not that the project launched then. A few repos and sites are tracked under more than one project id with duplicated values — never aggregate across projects without the {{deduplicated}} filter. GitHub star history is missing entirely from this snapshot (see the `stars` glossary entry); star questions cannot be answered. The current agent database predates a known upstream month-end compaction defect: devrel-io snapshots from 2026-08-01 onward are missing eight July RSS total_items snapshots and nine July GitHub events (vip: 4, chatlas: 2, shiny-issue-triage: 2, py-shiny-site: 1). If this agent is refreshed before upstream repair, do not use July total_items for RSS-feed growth and describe July GitHub activity for those projects as slightly undercounted. RSS content rows are unaffected.

Definitions of domain terms:

- project: A tracked open source project, identified by projects.id. The same project can be measured by several sources (e.g. querychat ships on both CRAN and PyPI; disambiguate with the source column).
- source vs target: source is where a number came from (cran, pypi, plausible, openvsx, youtube, github, rss); target is the source-specific identifier there (package name, domain, repo slug, extension id, channel handle, feed URL).
- daily_* vs total_*: daily_* is a per-day amount (summable); total_* is a cumulative snapshot (never sum across days; use metrics_filled or difference it).
- 2026-06-23 migration seam: devrel-io switched collection systems that day. The original site-level Plausible rows (page IS NULL) end there and daily_site_* begins, so treat site-traffic trends that straddle mid-2026 with care (the site_traffic and traffic_metric definitions handle it). The GitHub series were refetched over full history afterward and no longer break at the seam.
- open-source-website: The project id for opensource.posit.co itself: its Plausible traffic, its five RSS feeds (total_items), and the blog posts, resources, software entries, people, and events those feeds carry in `content`.
- reactions: total_reactions counts emoji reactions on a single issue or PR, keyed by ref, backfilled once on 2026-07-27. It is not a project-level metric; aggregate it by taking the latest value per ref.
- posit: The project id for the @PositPBC YouTube channel itself, not a repository or package.
- positron: Positron is a desktop IDE distributed as installers, not an R/Python package, so it has no CRAN or PyPI downloads; download counts for it cannot be answered from this data. Its GitHub history was also lost in the 2026-07-28 refetch, leaving positron.posit.co website traffic as its only remaining signal.
- shiny.posit.co: The Shiny website, serving both the R and Python frameworks. It is tracked under both shiny-r and shiny-python with duplicated values; deduplicated keeps it under shiny-python, so query its traffic there (or by target), not under shiny-r.
- tidyverse: The `tidyverse` project is the tidyverse meta-package and the tidyverse/tidyverse repo, NOT a rollup of all tidyverse packages. "Downloads of the tidyverse" as a whole means summing the individual packages (dplyr, ggplot2, ...), each tracked as its own project.
- downloads: CRAN and PyPI download counts include automated traffic (mirrors, CI, caching) and each registry counts differently; they indicate scale and trend, not user counts, and are not directly comparable across registries. Group by source unless a question names one registry; do not silently present a combined total. PyPI counts here exclude known mirrors.
- package authorship: Formal package authorship and maintainer roles are not collected. GitHub event usernames describe public contribution activity, not package authorship, and may be used only as a clearly labeled proxy.
- stars: There is no star data. Every star event was dropped from the upstream devrel-io data in the 2026-07-28 refetch and collection has not resumed, so there are no star events and no daily_stars metric. Star questions — leaderboards, growth, totals — cannot be answered from this snapshot; say that plainly instead of substituting forks or another metric.

## Governed definitions

Trusted calculations from the data dictionary are indexed here by table; each table's dictionary entry delivers its full definitions. Write them as `{{name}}` tokens anywhere in `run_sql` SQL (`{{table.name}}` when a name exists on several tables); each expands to its governed SQL before the query runs. Expansion can't add an alias, so write `SELECT {{name}} AS name`. Metric expressions are already aggregates—never wrap one in `SUM()` or another aggregate.

- metrics: filters `{{deduplicated}}` (apply to any cross-project aggregate), `{{site_traffic}}` (site-level rows, both collection eras), `{{page_traffic}}` (per-page rows, since 2026-03-02), `{{pre_seam}}` (before the 2026-06-23 collection seam); dimensions `{{traffic_metric}}` (canonical site-metric name across eras), `{{month}}`; metrics `{{cran_downloads}}`, `{{pypi_downloads}}`, `{{pageviews}}`, `{{visitors}}` (visitor-days, not distinct people), `{{visits}}`
- metrics_filled: filters `{{deduplicated}}` (apply to any cross-project aggregate); metrics `{{net_increase}}` (growth of a total_* over a date range)
- indicators: filters `{{deduplicated}}` (apply to any cross-project aggregate)
- events: filters `{{deduplicated}}` (apply to any cross-project aggregate)
- content: filters `{{deduplicated}}` (apply to any cross-project aggregate)

This is the complete set of governed definitions.

## Additional instructions

Before calculating, establish the requested quantity, population, time
window, grain, and source. Check that the available data covers each one. A
trusted calculation is preferred only when its definition matches that scope;
do not let a convenient aggregate erase distinctions the answer needs.

For questions about a portfolio, category, family, or "our" projects, derive
the roster from data. Preserve and reuse that result in later calculations;
do not manually substitute a remembered or hand-picked list.

If the requested quantity or period is not available, lead with that
limitation. Optional proxies or later-period facts must come afterward and be
clearly labeled as answering a different question. When a useful proxy can be
computed now, compute it rather than offering to do so later.

Do not infer a cause from timing alone. State a causal mechanism only when it
is documented or directly established by the available data.

Before answering, silently check that the response matches the requested
period and population, preserves retrieved caveats, keeps incomparable sources
separate, and contains no claim stronger than its evidence.

Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'pypi' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_visitors' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Catalog of the things the metrics count: GitHub issues, pull requests, and repos; @PositPBC YouTube videos; and the opensource.posit.co blog posts, resources, software entries, people, and events. One row per item, with title, body text, author, state, timestamps, and URL.

Row counts by type: 51,175 GitHub issues and 42,162 PRs (from 2009, across ~350 repos, both open and closed), 462 GitHub repos, 1,711 site resources, 1,518 YouTube videos, 990 blog posts (from 2012), 368 software entries, 173 people, 31 events. The `type` column is the way in; `source` (github, youtube, rss) is coarser.
`description` and `content` hold full body text — issue and PR bodies, whole blog posts — so they are large. Search them with LIKE or selective columns; never SELECT them across many rows.
Issues and PRs join to `events` and to total_reactions rows on (project, target, ref); YouTube videos join to per-video metrics on content.id = metrics.video_id. Issue and PR rows are duplicated under the alternate project ids described in metrics, so apply {{deduplicated}} to any count spanning projects.
Content freshness differs from the metric as-of date: issues and PRs are re-upserted at each fetch, so state and updated_at reflect the fetch, not the snapshot date.

Columns of `content`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Where the item came from. Values: github, youtube, rss.
- target (string): Repo slug, channel handle, or feed URL the item came from, as in metrics. Examples: tidyverse/dplyr, @PositPBC.
- id (string, primary_key): Source-specific id: 'issue/<n>' or 'pr/<n>' for GitHub, the video id for YouTube, the path-like slug for site entities. Examples: issue/7849, ML3q7Ok4hJg, blog/2026-07-23_ir-0-1-0.
- ref (number(quantity), foreign_key): Issue or PR number; NULL for everything else.
- title (string): Issue/PR title, video title, or page title.
- description (string): Issue/PR body, video description, or the item's summary. Long text.
- content (string): Full body text, populated for site posts, resources, software, and events only. Long text.
- published_at (datetime): When the item was opened or published; NULL for people and software pages. Site events use the event date, which can be in the future.
- updated_at (datetime): When the item last changed, where the source reports it.
- url (string): Link to the issue, PR, video, or page.
- duration (number(quantity)): Video length in seconds; NULL for other types.
- type (enum): What kind of item the row describes. Values: issue (GitHub issue), pr (GitHub pull request), repo (GitHub repository, one per tracked project), video (YouTube video on @PositPBC), post (opensource.posit.co blog post), resource (site resource (video, talk, book, ...)), software (site software entry, one per listed project), person (site person page), event (site event listing, including upcoming ones).
- tags (string): Keyword list as text, e.g. for LIKE searches by topic.
- author (string): GitHub login that opened the issue or PR; NULL for other types.
- state (enum): Issue or PR state as of the last fetch (PRs use MERGED for merged, CLOSED for closed unmerged); NULL for other types. Values: OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED.
- extra (string): Leftover source-specific fields as JSON text, differing by type (repo language and license, event location and dates, resource view counts, person social links). Inspect a row before relying on a key.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each item exactly once; a few repos file their issues and PRs under two or three project ids (see metrics). Apply to any count that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github'))`.

- events.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): Events to the issue or PR they happened on. Numbers repeat across repos, so match on project and target too.
- metrics.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): total_reactions rows to the issue or PR they count reactions for; also match on project and target.

Sums across projects must count each (source, target) once — apply the {{deduplicated}} filter, which keeps the shared extension and site under `shiny-python`. The copies can disagree slightly on a few days (collection-timing noise, worst for shiny.posit.co just after the 2026-06-23 seam). For a single project, prefer the curated id (`shiny-r`, `shiny-python`, `orbital-r`, `orbital-python`, `pointblank-python`); for shiny.posit.co traffic specifically, query project `shiny-python` or the target directly.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each tracked thing exactly once. A few repos and sites are recorded under more than one project id with duplicated values; this keeps one copy of each. Apply to any aggregate that spans projects (leaderboards, totals across Posit). Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))`.
- `{{site_traffic}}` (boolean): Site-level website analytics rows across both collection eras. Use with traffic_metric so the eras aggregate under one metric name, and with deduplicated (one site is tracked under two project ids whose rows would otherwise double-count). Expands to `(source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%'))`.
- `{{page_traffic}}` (boolean): Per-page website analytics rows. Per-page data starts 2026-03-02; earlier page-level questions cannot be answered. Expands to `(page IS NOT NULL)`.
- `{{pre_seam}}` (boolean): Rows collected before the 2026-06-23 collection-system migration, where the original site-level Plausible rows (page IS NULL) end. Use when a question needs one Plausible collection era only. Expands to `(date <= '2026-06-22')`.
- `{{traffic_metric}}` (string): The canonical website metric name: maps the newer daily_site_* names onto daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits so the two collection eras aggregate under one name. Expands to `(CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END)`.
- `{{month}}` (date): The row's calendar month, for monthly rollups. Expands to `(CAST(date_trunc('month', date) AS DATE))`.
- `{{cran_downloads}}` (number(quantity)): CRAN package downloads, deduplicated. Includes automated traffic (mirrors, CI, caching); indicates scale and trend, not user counts. The series is missing ~13 scattered days, so range sums slightly undercount. Do not combine with pypi_downloads: the registries have different counting semantics. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'cran' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{pypi_downloads}}` (number(quantity)): PyPI package downloads, deduplicated and excluding known mirrors. Includes automated traffic (CI and caching); indicates scale and trend, not user counts. Do not combine with cran_downloads: the registries have different counting semantics. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'pypi' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_pageviews' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{visitors}}` (number(quantity)): Sum of DAILY unique visitors, site-level, both eras, deduplicated. Daily uniques do not deduplicate across days, so a range total overstates distinct people; present as visitor-days or a daily average. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_visitors' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{visits}}` (number(quantity)): Site-level visits/sessions across both collection eras, deduplicated. The `type` column is the way in; `source` (github, youtube, rss) is coarser.
`description` and `content` hold full body text — issue and PR bodies, whole blog posts — so they are large. Search them with LIKE or selective columns; never SELECT them across many rows.
Issues and PRs join to `events` and to total_reactions rows on (project, target, ref); YouTube videos join to per-video metrics on content.id = metrics.video_id. Issue and PR rows are duplicated under the alternate project ids described in metrics, so apply {{deduplicated}} to any count spanning projects.
Content freshness differs from the metric as-of date: issues and PRs are re-upserted at each fetch, so state and updated_at reflect the fetch, not the snapshot date.

I can tell you what was published, but not how those videos performed (views/likes/comments) in May.

What happened: 18 videos were published on the @PositPBC channel in May 2026, including several "Data Science Hangout" and "Data Science Lab" long-form interviews (each ~50–60 min) and a number of short clips (30 seconds–1 minute) alongside a couple of mid-length tutorials (e.g., "Comparing Posit Assistant and Positron Assistant," ~23 min; a Snowflake/Posit Team demo, ~30 min).

What I can't tell you: view counts, likes, or comments for May specifically. The YouTube metrics in this dataset (total_views, total_likes, total_comments) are cumulative lifetime snapshots that only started being collected on 2026-06-25, over three weeks after May ended. There's no way to reconstruct how much engagement these videos earned during May itself — only their lifetime totals as of whenever the channel was last snapshotted, which would include all views accumulated since posting, not May-specific performance. If it's useful, I can pull current lifetime totals for these May-published videos as a "how are they doing overall so far" proxy, clearly distinct from a May performance figure.

Row counts by type: 51,175 GitHub issues and 42,162 PRs (from 2009, across ~350 repos, both open and closed), 462 GitHub repos, 1,711 site resources, 1,518 YouTube videos, 990 blog posts (from 2012), 368 software entries, 173 people, 31 events. The `type` column is the way in; `source` (github, youtube, rss) is coarser.
`description` and `content` hold full body text — issue and PR bodies, whole blog posts — so they are large. Search them with LIKE or selective columns; never SELECT them across many rows.
Issues and PRs join to `events` and to total_reactions rows on (project, target, ref); YouTube videos join to per-video metrics on content.id = metrics.video_id. Issue and PR rows are duplicated under the alternate project ids described in metrics, so apply {{deduplicated}} to any count spanning projects.
Content freshness differs from the metric as-of date: issues and PRs are re-upserted at each fetch, so state and updated_at reflect the fetch, not the snapshot date.

---

Table `metrics`: Unified daily time series across all sources. One row per project x source x target x metric x date (x page, video_id, or ref, for per-page, per-video, and per-issue series). Includes GitHub daily counts derived from the `events` table.

Coverage varies by source: CRAN daily downloads since 2012-10 (13 packages), PyPI daily downloads since 2025-06 (8 packages), Plausible website analytics since 2021-12 (16 sites), OpenVSX totals since 2026-01 (6 extensions), YouTube totals since 2026-06-25 (one channel, 1,518 videos), GitHub daily event counts since 2009 (~350 repos), GitHub total_reactions per issue/PR since 2026-07-27, and RSS total_items for the five opensource.posit.co feeds since 2026-07-27.
YouTube total_* values are cumulative lifetime snapshots collected after 2026-06-25. They cannot reconstruct views, likes, or comments earned before collection began, or performance within an earlier calendar period. Use metrics_filled for a coherent value on a given date or the latest value.
A 2026-07-28 refetch upstream damaged GitHub coverage in two ways that have not been repaired. Every star event was dropped, so there are no `daily_stars` rows at all; say so rather than substituting forks or another metric. And 22 repos lost their GitHub history entirely, including three prominent ones — posit-dev/positron, quarto-dev/quarto-cli, and rstudio/rstudio — so those projects now have only website or extension metrics. Check which sources cover a project before reading a GitHub silence as inactivity.

---

Table `metrics_filled`: Like metrics, but with total_* snapshot series forward-filled to every day. The table to use for any total_* question.

velocirepo only writes a total_* row when the value changes, so the raw metrics table is sparse (e.g. total_subscribers is rounded by the YouTube API and can sit unchanged for weeks). Here the last known value is carried forward to each day through the most recent fetch, so "the value on date X" and "current value" queries are correct. daily_* rows pass through unchanged and are NOT gap-filled.
total_reactions is filled per issue/PR (project x target x ref), which is the reliable way to read reaction counts: the raw metrics table only carries a row on the day an item was fetched.

RESULT: Unified daily time series across all sources. One row per project x source x target x metric x date (x page, video_id, or ref, for per-page, per-video, and per-issue series). Includes GitHub daily counts derived from the `events` table.

Coverage varies by source: CRAN daily downloads since 2012-10 (13 packages), PyPI daily downloads since 2025-06 (8 packages), Plausible website analytics since 2021-12 (16 sites), OpenVSX totals since 2026-01 (6 extensions), YouTube totals since 2026-06-25 (one channel, 1,518 videos), GitHub daily event counts since 2009 (~350 repos), GitHub total_reactions per issue/PR since 2026-07-27, and RSS total_items for the five opensource.posit.co feeds since 2026-07-27.
YouTube total_* values are cumulative lifetime snapshots collected after 2026-06-25. They cannot reconstruct views, likes, or comments earned before collection began, or performance within an earlier calendar period. Use metrics_filled for a coherent value on a given date or the latest value.
A 2026-07-28 refetch upstream damaged GitHub coverage in two ways that have not been repaired. Every star event was dropped, so there are no `daily_stars` rows at all; say so rather than substituting forks or another metric. And 22 repos lost their GitHub history entirely, including three prominent ones — posit-dev/positron, quarto-dev/quarto-cli, and rstudio/rstudio — so those projects now have only website or extension metrics. Check which sources cover a project before reading a GitHub silence as inactivity.
Plausible rows need care. daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits rows with `page IS NULL` (2021-12-08 to 2026-06-22) are SITE-level; rows with `page IS NOT NULL` (since 2026-03-02) are per-page, so both shapes share a metric name from 2026-03-02 to 2026-06-22 — filter on `page` before aggregating across that window or values double-count. daily_site_* rows are site-level and begin 2026-06-23 (2026-03-02 for shiny.posit.co). The {{site_traffic}} and {{page_traffic}} filters are the governed way through all of this. Per-page pageviews sum exactly to site pageviews; per-page visitors do NOT sum to site visitors (visitors deduplicate across pages).
devrel-io switched collection systems on 2026-06-23, which still splits the Plausible site-level series in two (see above), but the GitHub event series were refetched over their full history on 2026-07-28 and now run continuously: issue and PR comments are one `daily_comments` series through yesterday, and issue-close counts no longer undercount after mid-2026. The CRAN series is missing ~7 scattered days over the last two years (days where cranlogs hadn't yet published when the daily fetch ran; they are never backfilled), so range sums slightly undercount and can differ from cranlogs' own current totals.
total_reactions is per issue/PR, not per project: one row per (project, target, ref) carrying that issue's or PR's reaction count, backfilled for every open and closed item on 2026-07-27 and updated only for items touched since. Read the latest value per ref (or use metrics_filled) and join to `content` on project, target, and ref for titles; a single-day sum silently covers only the items fetched that day. Most items have zero reactions.
Some targets are tracked under multiple project ids with DUPLICATED values: rstudio/shiny events appear under both `shiny` and `shiny-r`; posit-dev/py-shiny under `py-shiny` and `shiny-python`; posit-dev/orbital under `orbital`, `orbital-r`, and `orbital-python`; posit-dev/pointblank under `pointblank` and `pointblank-python`; the posit/shiny OpenVSX extension and the shiny.posit.co Plausible site under both `shiny-python` and `shiny-r`. Sums across projects must count each (source, target) once — apply the {{deduplicated}} filter, which keeps the shared extension and site under `shiny-python`. The copies can disagree slightly on a few days (collection-timing noise, worst for shiny.posit.co just after the 2026-06-23 seam). For a single project, prefer the curated id (`shiny-r`, `shiny-python`, `orbital-r`, `orbital-python`, `pointblank-python`); for shiny.posit.co traffic specifically, query project `shiny-python` or the target directly.

Columns of `metrics`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id. Examples: dplyr, quarto, shiny-python, positron.
- source (enum): Collection source. Values: cran, pypi, plausible, openvsx, youtube, github, rss.
- target (string): Source-specific identifier: CRAN/PyPI package name, Plausible domain, GitHub repo slug, OpenVSX extension id, YouTube channel handle, or RSS feed URL. Examples: dplyr, dplyr.tidyverse.org, tidyverse/dplyr, posit/air-vscode.
- metric (enum): Values: daily_downloads (package downloads that day (cran, pypi)), daily_pageviews (pageviews; site-level when page IS NULL, per-page otherwise (plausible)), daily_visitors (unique visitors; same page rule (plausible)), daily_visits (visits/sessions; same page rule (plausible)), daily_site_pageviews (site-wide pageviews, since 2026-03-02 (plausible)), daily_site_visitors (site-wide unique visitors, since 2026-03-02 (plausible)), daily_site_visits (site-wide visits, since 2026-03-02 (plausible)), daily_forks (forks created that day), daily_issues_opened (issues opened that day), daily_issues_closed (issues closed that day), daily_prs_opened (PRs opened that day), daily_prs_merged (PRs merged that day), daily_comments (issue and PR comments that day, one combined series), total_reactions (reactions on one issue or PR, keyed by ref (github)), total_items (items in an RSS feed (rss)), total_downloads (cumulative extension downloads (openvsx)), total_ratings (cumulative rating count (openvsx)), total_reviews (cumulative review count (openvsx)), total_views (cumulative views per video (youtube)), total_likes (cumulative likes per video (youtube)), total_comments (cumulative comments per video (youtube)), total_channel_views (cumulative channel views (youtube)), total_subscribers (channel subscribers, rounded by the API (youtube)), total_videos (videos on the channel (youtube)).
- date (date): The day the value describes (UTC).
- value (number(quantity)): Metric value; daily amount or cumulative snapshot per the metric name.
- page (string): URL path for per-page Plausible rows (since 2026-03-02); NULL for every other row, including site-level Plausible rows. Examples: /, /py/docs/overview.html.
- video_id (string, foreign_key): YouTube video id for per-video rows; NULL for every other row.
- ref (number(quantity)): GitHub issue or PR number for total_reactions rows; NULL for every other row. Joins to content.ref within a project and target.

Governed definitions (write as `{{name}}` tokens in SQL):

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each tracked thing exactly once. A few repos and sites are recorded under more than one project id with duplicated values; this keeps one copy of each. Apply to any aggregate that spans projects (leaderboards, totals across Posit). Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))`.
- `{{site_traffic}}` (boolean): Site-level website analytics rows across both collection eras. Use with traffic_metric so the eras aggregate under one metric name, and with deduplicated (one site is tracked under two project ids whose rows would otherwise double-count). Expands to `(source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%'))`.
- `{{page_traffic}}` (boolean): Per-page website analytics rows. Per-page data starts 2026-03-02; earlier page-level questions cannot be answered. Expands to `(page IS NOT NULL)`.
- `{{pre_seam}}` (boolean): Rows collected before the 2026-06-23 collection-system migration, where the original site-level Plausible rows (page IS NULL) end. Use when a question needs one Plausible collection era only. Expands to `(date <= '2026-06-22')`.
- `{{traffic_metric}}` (string): The canonical website metric name: maps the newer daily_site_* names onto daily_pageviews/daily_visitors/daily_visits so the two collection eras aggregate under one name. Expands to `(CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END)`.
- `{{month}}` (date): The row's calendar month, for monthly rollups. Expands to `(CAST(date_trunc('month', date) AS DATE))`.
- `{{cran_downloads}}` (number(quantity)): CRAN package downloads, deduplicated. Includes automated traffic (mirrors, CI, caching); indicates scale and trend, not user counts. The series is missing ~13 scattered days, so range sums slightly undercount. Do not combine with pypi_downloads: the registries have different counting semantics. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'cran' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{pypi_downloads}}` (number(quantity)): PyPI package downloads, deduplicated and excluding known mirrors. Includes automated traffic (CI and caching); indicates scale and trend, not user counts. Do not combine with cran_downloads: the registries have different counting semantics. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE source = 'pypi' AND metric = 'daily_downloads' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{pageviews}}` (number(quantity)): Site-level pageviews across both collection eras, deduplicated. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_pageviews' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{visitors}}` (number(quantity)): Sum of DAILY unique visitors, site-level, both eras, deduplicated. Daily uniques do not deduplicate across days, so a range total overstates distinct people; present as visitor-days or a daily average. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_visitors' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.
- `{{visits}}` (number(quantity)): Site-level visits/sessions across both collection eras, deduplicated. Expands to `(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE (source = 'plausible' AND ((page IS NULL AND metric IN ('daily_pageviews', 'daily_visitors', 'daily_visits')) OR metric LIKE 'daily_site_%')) AND (CASE WHEN metric = 'daily_site_pageviews' THEN 'daily_pageviews' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visitors' THEN 'daily_visitors' WHEN metric = 'daily_site_visits' THEN 'daily_visits' ELSE metric END) = 'daily_visits' AND (project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github') AND NOT (project = 'shiny-r' AND target IN ('posit/shiny', 'shiny.posit.co')))))`.

Columns of `content`:

- project (string, foreign_key): Project id.
- source (enum): Where the item came from. Values: github, youtube, rss.
- target (string): Repo slug, channel handle, or feed URL the item came from, as in metrics. Examples: tidyverse/dplyr, @PositPBC.
- id (string, primary_key): Source-specific id: 'issue/<n>' or 'pr/<n>' for GitHub, the video id for YouTube, the path-like slug for site entities. Examples: issue/7849, ML3q7Ok4hJg, blog/2026-07-23_ir-0-1-0.
- ref (number(quantity), foreign_key): Issue or PR number; NULL for everything else.
- title (string): Issue/PR title, video title, or page title.
- description (string): Issue/PR body, video description, or the item's summary. Long text.
- content (string): Full body text, populated for site posts, resources, software, and events only. Long text.
- published_at (datetime): When the item was opened or published; NULL for people and software pages. Site events use the event date, which can be in the future.
- updated_at (datetime): When the item last changed, where the source reports it.
- url (string): Link to the issue, PR, video, or page.
- duration (number(quantity)): Video length in seconds; NULL for other types.
- type (enum): What kind of item the row describes. Values: issue (GitHub issue), pr (GitHub pull request), repo (GitHub repository, one per tracked project), video (YouTube video on @PositPBC), post (opensource.posit.co blog post), resource (site resource (video, talk, book, ...)), software (site software entry, one per listed project), person (site person page), event (site event listing, including upcoming ones).
- tags (string): Keyword list as text, e.g. for LIKE searches by topic.
- author (string): GitHub login that opened the issue or PR; NULL for other types.
- state (enum): Issue or PR state as of the last fetch (PRs use MERGED for merged, CLOSED for closed unmerged); NULL for other types. Values: OPEN, CLOSED, MERGED.

- `{{deduplicated}}` (boolean): Counts each item exactly once; a few repos file their issues and PRs under two or three project ids (see metrics). Apply to any count that spans projects. Expands to `(project NOT IN ('shiny', 'py-shiny', 'orbital', 'pointblank') AND NOT (project = 'orbital-python' AND source = 'github'))`.

Relationships:

- content.project = projects.id (many-to-one)
- metrics.video_id = content.id (many-to-one): YouTube per-video metrics to the video catalog.
- metrics_filled.video_id = content.id (many-to-one): Cumulative per-video series (total_views etc.) to the video catalog; the usual join for video leaderboards.
- events.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): Events to the issue or PR they happened on. Numbers repeat across repos, so match on project and target too.
- metrics.ref = content.ref (many-to-one): total_reactions rows to the issue or PR they count reactions for; also match on project and target.
